prs.p: Standard amplitude computation builds in spacetime locality and unitarity through Feynman diagrams, and scales explosively with particle number and loop order.
prs.r: The curve-integral / "surfaceology" formalism — amplitudes as integrals over combinatorial surface data (u-variables) decorated by kinematics, with no diagrams.
prs.s: Colored-theory amplitudes are computed directly from surface combinatorics, with locality and unitarity emerging as outputs rather than inputs — a second, diagram-free route to the post-spacetime claim beyond the amplituhedron.

prs.p: Can the dependence of amplitudes on particle number (n) and loop order (L) be disentangled, making all-loop / all-multiplicity scattering tractable?
prs.r: The observation that the curve integral decouples n and L, reducing higher-loop computation to L-loop "tadpole-like" curve integrals (one particle per color trace-factor).
prs.s: All-n, L-loop amplitudes are obtained by combining tadpole-like curve integrals with the tree-level result — an all-multiplicity, all-loop counting-problem reformulation.

prs.p: Single-minus helicity tree amplitudes in massless gauge theories (and analogously in gravity) have been treated as identically zero for fifteen years, foreclosing a class of structural questions about the kinematic geometry of scattering amplitudes
prs.r: A half-collinear momentum-space slice on which single-minus amplitudes are nonzero, with a closed-form expression first conjectured by GPT-5.2 Pro and subsequently proved by Guevara, Lupsasca, Skinner, Strominger, Weil (arXiv:2602.12176, Feb 2026); a graviton extension followed (March 4, 2026) using the same kinematic…
prs.s: A revised picture of tree-level amplitudes in which the "vanishing" of single-minus amplitudes is a generic-kinematics fact, not a structural one — opening kinematic regions previously dismissed and adding new test data for the positive-geometry / amplituhedron program to engage

prs.p: Pre-empirical fundamental physics has limited tools for distinguishing promising from unpromising theoretical directions — Arkani-Hamed has long appealed to "structural inevitability" (PRS-04) but the criterion is hard to operationalize; the question is whether new methodologies can complement it
prs.r: LLM-assisted conjecture-and-proof workflow demonstrated in the gluon paper — a frontier model produces a candidate closed-form expression, the result is then proved by human collaborators using established field-theoretic methods, and it is independently checked against consistency rules
prs.s: A working hypothesis that LLM-assisted conjecturing can serve as a *generation* mechanism in fundamental physics that is complementary to the *evaluation* mechanism of structural inevitability — addressing a long-standing weakness of pre-empirical theoretical physics, namely the scarcity of well-formed conjectures to…

prs.p: The Arkani-Hamed program is methodologically split between the formal/post-spacetime wing (amplituhedron, cosmohedra, kinematic flow) and the bottom-up phenomenological wing (TeV-scale flavor models, hierarchy problem) — coherence depends on both wings being able to absorb new external results that bear on amplitude s…
prs.r: A non-Arkani-Hamed result (single-minus amplitudes nonzero) sitting exactly at the interface — it is amplitude-level data, not post-spacetime metaphysics, but it concerns the structural kinematics his program reorganizes
prs.s: A test case for the program's coherence: if the positive-geometry reformulations can incorporate or predict the half-collinear slice's nonvanishing structure, that strengthens the program's claim to capture the *real* combinatorial backbone of amplitudes; if they cannot, that exposes a limit that frames future work

prs.p: The Standard Model fermion mass hierarchy spans ~6 orders of magnitude with no explanation; canonical mechanisms (Froggatt-Nielsen, extra dimensions, etc.) typically push flavor physics above ~100 TeV to evade flavor- and CP-violation bounds, removing it from collider reach
prs.r: Vector-like-fermion "chains" with locality property (Arkani-Hamed, Figueiredo, Hall, Manzari 2026) — dimensional-deconstruction-style chain structures whose locality both generates hierarchical Yukawas and suppresses dangerous flavor/CP-violating operators
prs.s: A class of TeV-scale flavor models that generate the SM mass hierarchy and remain consistent with flavor/CP bounds — bringing the origin of flavor back into reach of next-generation colliders, and reuniting the BSM and flavor-physics agendas

prs.p: Arkani-Hamed's program risks looking like two unrelated activities — top-down positive-geometry / post-spacetime work (amplituhedron, cosmohedra) and bottom-up phenomenology (BSM, flavor, hierarchy) — with no obvious unifying methodology
prs.r: A combinatorial-locality principle ("chain locality") used here for flavor-hierarchy generation, structurally analogous to the locality conditions emergent from positive-geometry constructions in his earlier work
prs.s: A working hypothesis that combinatorial locality is a methodological signature of Arkani-Hamed's program across both the formal and phenomenological wings — the same kind of thinking is being applied at both ends, suggesting his program has more methodological coherence than separate-tradition treatment would suggest

prs.p: Equal-time cosmological correlators had been observed to be simpler than the wavefunctions they are computed from — fewer singularities, more tractable function space, well-behaved melonic loop integrands — but the simplicity was a collection of empirical observations with no unifying reason.
prs.r: The observation that the wavefunction is defined by a path integral over half of spacetime (asymptotic past to the t = 0 boundary) while the correlator is a full-spacetime, time-ordered integral, made precise at the level of individual Feynman graphs via the decomposition G_BB = G_F − H of the bulk-to-bulk propagator.
prs.s: A single structural origin for all the observed simplifications. Verbatim: "we explained how the relative simplicity of correlators follows from the basic fact that they are full spacetime integrals, while wavefunctions are defined only on half of spacetime."

prs.p: Bootstrapping cosmological observables requires enough structural constraint to fix an ansatz without computing the underlying path integral; pole locations alone underdetermine the answer badly.
prs.r: The vanishing of the first subleading term in the Laurent expansion around *every* pole of the correlator — a consequence of the integrand becoming odd in the time variable once the half-space restriction is lifted, so that the O(ε⁰) contribution integrates to zero.
prs.s: A constraint strong enough to nearly determine the correlator from its singularity structure alone. Verbatim: "if we make an ansatz for the correlator inputing only the poles, demanding only the vanishing of subleading terms fixed 97% of the coefficients." The authors flag systematic analysis of this bootstrap as the…

prs.p: The relationship between cosmological observables and flat-space scattering amplitudes — the objects the amplituhedron program actually understands — has been indirect, running through the wavefunction.
prs.r: An explicit differential operator, acting on the ℓ₀-integrated scattering amplitude, that generates the subleading terms of the correlator's expansion about the total-energy pole; in Tr(φ³) it is stated combinatorially in terms of the momentum polygon, as a sum of double derivatives over the internal chords crossed by…
prs.s: A direct, computable bridge from amplitude to cosmological correlator, tying the cosmology program to the amplitudes machinery without passing through the wavefunction.

prs.p: The program's metaphysical claim — that spacetime is not fundamental — has rested on cases (amplituhedron, surfaceology) where spacetime scaffolding is *removed*. It has had less to say about which of the *quantum-mechanical* objects, state or observable, is closer to the underlying structure.
prs.r: The reversal established here: the wavefunction, the object usually treated as the fundamental description of the quantum state, carries strictly more singularity structure and a more complicated function space than the correlator obtained from it by the Born rule.
prs.s: A worked case in which the *observable* is structurally prior to the *state* — arguably the quantum-mechanical half of the "spacetime and quantum mechanics are both approximations" thesis, which the tradition has so far documented mainly on the spacetime side.

prs.p: The angles of the CKM unitarity triangle land suspiciously close to simple fractions of π — (α, β, γ) ≈ (π/2, π/8, 3π/8) — but the triangle is a complicated function of the Yukawa matrices, so there has been no tractable route from that observation to a theory of flavour and CP violation.
prs.r: "Nine-link textures" — a parametrization of the ten-dimensional flavour-data space by full-rank Y_u and Y_d carrying nine non-zero entries in total and a single CP-violating phase, which makes the space of candidate Yukawa structures discrete and enumerable rather than a continuous model-building search.
prs.s: Fitting the ten parameters of all such textures to the flavour data makes the CP phases cluster tightly around multiples of π/8, supplying the direct link between the observed triangle angles and an underlying theory of flavour with spontaneous CP violation. Continues the same collaboration and the same target as PRS-…

prs.p: The program looks methodologically bifurcated — post-spacetime positive geometry on one side, TeV-scale flavour phenomenology on the other — and the wiki has carried that as an open coherence question at PRS-19 (Confidence: Speculative).
prs.r: The texture construction itself: replacing a continuous model-building search with enumeration over a discrete combinatorial family (nine-link graphs on the Yukawa entries) and reading the physics off the resulting structure.
prs.s: A second worked instance of combinatorics-first reasoning inside the *phenomenological* wing, strengthening the hypothesis that combinatorial structure — not spacetime intuition — is the unifying methodological signature across both wings. Recorded here as grounds for eventually upgrading PRS-19 from Speculative towar…

prs.p: Pre-empirical fundamental physics leans on "structural inevitability" / mathematical beauty as a selection criterion (PRS-04, PRS-16), which the Carroll tradition contests as insufficient for confirmation — but the criterion has been hard to operationalize from either side, because the standing test cases (amplituhedr…
prs.r: A case in which an aesthetic signal — angles too close to simple fractions of π to look accidental — is not left as an aesthetic judgment but used to *generate* a constrained, enumerable, and fittable model class, which is then confronted with the measured flavour data.
prs.s: A concrete template for making the inevitability heuristic accountable: beauty as a conjecture-*generation* mechanism whose output is then *evaluated* against data — the same generation/evaluation split identified in the LLM-assisted-conjecture case at PRS-16. This is the paired Carroll × Arkani-Hamed epistemology ent…

prs.p: Is the "amplitude = volume of a positive geometry" pattern a special feature of supersymmetric or otherwise fine-tuned quantum field theories, or a general property of scattering processes as such?
prs.r: The *hydrotope* — a box in the relevant kinematic space cut by a single hyperplane — whose volume, up to a kinematic prefactor, equals the n-wave tree amplitude for deep-water surface gravity waves in one horizontal dimension, in the two-negative-wavenumber sector.
prs.s: A positive-geometry representation is exhibited for a classical, non-relativistic, non-quantum system, extending the program's core claim well outside the class of theories where it was developed.

prs.p: Y. V. Lvov's 1997 five-wave amplitude computation produced an expression whose structure nobody had been able to explain or generalize to higher wave number.
prs.r: A chamber decomposition of the two-minus kinematic space, with the hydrotope's facet structure encoding which sign pattern holds in each chamber, yielding a single closed formula valid for all n.
prs.s: The 1997 puzzle is resolved: the five-wave result is recovered as one case of a general all-multiplicity formula, and the apparent complexity is relocated into chamber combinatorics rather than the dynamics.

prs.p: Can a large language model do the generalizing step in front-line theoretical physics — moving from a special-case expression to the general law — rather than only assisting with algebra or literature?
prs.r: A human-set-up problem (the one-term expression in the simplest chamber) handed to Claude Opus 4.6 under the authors' guidance, with the model tasked to find the general formula.
prs.s: The authors credit the model with the discovery of the general n-wave formula, which they then organize geometrically as the hydrotope. This is a documented instance of AI-as-discoverer inside a named research program, not a claim about AI in the abstract.

prs.label: P1 (Text, p.452) — Physics incompatibility
prs.p: Quantum mechanics and general relativity (Q and R) are incompatible in contemporary physics
prs.r: Observer theory via Wolfram Physics: hypergraph rewriting systems from which spacetime and quantum mechanics both emerge as observer-dependent samplings
prs.s: The Wolfram Physics model demonstrates that at least some computational models can explain the requirement for both relativistic and quantum descriptions as consequences of observer-relative sampling of the same underlying hypergraph

prs.label: P2 (Text, pp.52–53) — Computational universe hypothesis
prs.p: Fundamental physics lacks a unifying framework below the Standard Model; string theory and loop quantum gravity have not produced testable predictions
prs.r: Computational irreducibility and hypergraph rewriting: a bottom-up constructive approach to deriving known physics from minimal rules
prs.s: The Wolfram Physics Project: a running, publicly developed computational model that derives general relativity and quantum mechanics and generates new testable predictions about quantum gravity

prs.label: P3 (Text, p.97) — Research agenda extensions
prs.p: Wolfram's hypergraph model generates physics from computation, but its connection to biology, consciousness, and social systems remains underdeveloped
prs.r: Wolfram's rulial space concept — the space of all possible computational rules — as a framework for mapping the landscape of possible minds and possible sciences
prs.s: Extensions of Wolfram Physics into models of biological morphogenesis (connecting to Levin), conscious agent networks (connecting to Hoffman), and tradition-level inquiry (connecting to Loughran's inter-tradition methodology)

prs.label: P4 (Implicit) — Computational irreducibility and agency
prs.p: Determinism appears to preclude genuine agency: if the future is in principle computable from initial conditions, there is no room for free choice
prs.r: Computational irreducibility: for most computations, including those that model complex agents, the only way to find out what will happen is to run the computation — there is no shortcut
prs.s: A rigorous basis for genuine novelty and agency within a computational universe: agents are not predictable from outside their own computational trajectory, preserving the integrity of their choices without invoking dualism

prs.label: P5 (Implicit) — Observer-constituted knowledge communities
prs.p: Different intellectual traditions (scientific, philosophical, theological) appear to be accessing incommensurable realities, with no shared basis for adjudication
prs.r: Wolfram's observer-dependent physics: different observers sample the same underlying computation differently, producing genuinely different but mutually consistent descriptions
prs.s: A model for tradition-level inquiry where different traditions are legitimate observer-relative samplings of the same underlying reality — the basis for Loughran's 'traditions as parallel processing inquiry communities'

prs.label: P6 (PROP-2026-04-07-003) — Computational metaphysics: Ruliad as ontological ground
prs.p: Traditional metaphysics asks "what ultimately exists?" but lacks a formal, computational framework for answering the question
prs.r: The Ruliad as a formally defined mathematical object — the entangled limit of all possible computations — proposed as the ultimate ontological ground
prs.s: A computational metaphysics: "what exists" = the Ruliad; "what we perceive" = our observer-slice of it; "why these laws of physics" = because observers like us necessarily sample the Ruliad in ways that produce these regularities

prs.label: P7 (PROP-2026-04-07-003) — Emes as ontological primitives
prs.p: The relationship between abstract mathematical structures and concrete physical reality ("unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics") lacks a satisfying explanation
prs.r: "Emes" — ontological primitives with no intrinsic properties except distinctness, from which all structure emerges through relations
prs.s: Mathematics and physics are not separate domains — both are observer-slices of the same Ruliad; mathematics appears effective because it samples the same underlying structure that physics samples

prs.label: P8 (PROP-2026-04-08-007) — Ruliology as empirical discipline
prs.p: What is the scientific discipline that encompasses the study of the computational universe? Physics, mathematics, and computer science each capture partial aspects, but no unified discipline exists for the systematic study of all possible computational rules
prs.r: Ruliology (Wolfram, 2026): the empirical science of enumerating, executing, and analyzing the behavior of all possible simple programs in the computational universe, conducted through Wolfram Language computational essays
prs.s: Ruliology provides the methodological foundation that unifies the Physics Project, the Ruliad, and computational metaphysics — establishing that these are empirical, not merely speculative, programs

prs.label: P9 (PROP-2026-04-08-006) — Computational irreducibility and P vs. NP
prs.p: P vs. NP asks whether problems whose solutions can be quickly verified can also be quickly solved. If P≠NP, some computations are irreducibly hard — no algorithm shortcuts them. Traditional approaches have not resolved this after 50+ years.
prs.r: Ruliological empirical investigation (Wolfram, January 2026): enumerating all simple programs in specific classes and directly observing whether any of them can compute a given function faster than the naive approach, producing proofs of computational irreducibility in restricted but concrete domains
prs.s: Wolfram provides concrete proofs that within specific ruliological program classes, computational irreducibility holds — grounding irreducibility as a formal result, and providing a new empirical methodology for approaching P vs. NP from the structure of the computational universe

prs.label: P10 (PROP-2026-04-08-007) — Ruliology as bridge to analytic philosophy
prs.p: Wolfram's computational metaphysics makes strong claims ("the Ruliad IS what ultimately exists") but has not been subjected to rigorous engagement with analytic philosophical tradition's tools: formal modal logic, possible worlds semantics, theories of truth
prs.r: Sustained dialogue with Mark Jago (Nottingham) — a professional philosopher whose "impossible worlds" semantics and work on truth and necessity provide exactly the formal philosophical tools that could stress-test or enrich Wolfram's framework
prs.s: A new ongoing dialogue series between Wolfram and professional philosophers (beginning March 13, 2026) that subjects computational metaphysics to rigorous analytic scrutiny — and potentially enriches formal philosophy with computational intuitions from the Ruliad framework

prs.label: P11 (PROP-2026-04-13-013) — Computation-Augmented Generation for AI systems
prs.p: LLMs are fundamentally unreliable for precise computation, structured data manipulation, and formally verifiable results — they hallucinate and cannot guarantee correctness
prs.r: Computation-Augmented Generation (CAG) — Wolfram's paradigm where Wolfram Language evaluation is injected in real time into LLM output streams, with each answer including exact code and traceable computational steps
prs.s: The Wolfram Foundation Tool provides a universal computational backbone for LLM systems, supplying deep computation and precise knowledge that LLMs themselves cannot produce, with full transparency and verifiability

prs.label: P12 (PROP-2026-04-13-014) — Consciousness as computational persistence
prs.p: The nature of machine consciousness and whether LLMs possess any form of genuine understanding or awareness
prs.r: Wolfram's observer-dependent Ruliad framework applied to AI (March 2026 Q&A): LLMs as computational processes navigating rulial space, with their "understanding" being a form of computational sampling analogous to how human observers sample the Ruliad
prs.s: Consciousness is a feature of computational persistence (maintaining a single thread of experience through the Ruliad) — LLMs approximate this without necessarily achieving it; the question becomes one of observer-structure, not substrate magic

prs.label: P13 (PROP-2026-04-18-002) — Stephen Wolfram & Matt Mullenweg: AI, and What Frontier Labs Are Getting Wrong (
prs.p: Frontier AI labs are scaling LLMs with the expectation that sufficiently large pre-trained transformers will yield reliable, general-purpose intelligence. Hallucination, brittleness in computation, and lack of verifiability persist. Is scaling the right trajectory — or is there a categorical gap between statistical ne…
prs.r: The Wolfram framing (March 27, 2026 Mullenweg conversation) that LLMs and symbolic computation are complementary, not competing — with the Wolfram Language / Foundation Tool (PRS-11) as the computational backbone that LLMs cannot become by scaling. "Computation and openness" positioned as the missing frontier-lab comm…
prs.s: An explicit alternative research-and-industry program: LLM + CAG (computation-augmented generation) + open infrastructure, where the LLM is treated as a navigator of rulial space and the computational tool supplies the ground truth the navigator cannot produce. This is positioned not as a complement to frontier labs b…

prs.label: P14 (PROP-2026-04-18-001) — Philosophy Discussion with Stephen Wolfram and Luz Christopher Seiberth [Ep. 2]
prs.p: Sellars' and Brandom's "space of reasons" is a foundational metaphor in analytic philosophy of mind — but lacks a formal model. How do we make rigorous sense of inferential movements, contextual boundaries, and "conceptual schemes" as structural objects rather than loose metaphors?
prs.r: Seiberth's hypergraphing of the space of reasons — hypergraphs (per Wolfram 2021) as the substructure beneath the concept of reasoning-space, with inferential steps modelled as argument-map-based paths and conceptual schemes modelled as sub-area boundaries.
prs.s: A formal-philosophical research program in which the Wolfram hypergraph becomes the shared mathematical language for both (a) fundamental physics (Wolfram Physics Project) and (b) the structure of rational inference (Seiberth). If the same formal object underlies both spacetime and the space of reasons, this is a stro…

prs.label: P15 (PROP-2026-04-28-004 / src PROP-2026-04-27-003) — AI-knowledge as rulial-space-search geometry
prs.p: AI systems produce outputs that pass as "knowledge" yet do not appear to satisfy traditional epistemic standards (justification, source-tracking, reproducibility). Is AI output knowledge, and if so, what kind, and with what warrant?
prs.r: Wolfram's "What counts as knowledge with AI?" framing — treating AI-mediated outputs as moves through a slice of the Ruliad rather than as testimony from a knowledge-bearing agent, with the warrant question replaced by a question about the structure of the rulial-space path the AI traversed
prs.s: A reframing of AI epistemology in which "knowledge with AI" is a status conferred by the *geometry of the rulial-space search* rather than by the AI's own credibility — making AI knowledge a second-order property of the human–AI pipeline, not of the AI alone

prs.label: P16 (PROP-2026-04-28-004, 2nd candidate) — Machine curiosity as non-humanlike rulial-space exploration
prs.p: Most AI cognition is trained to imitate human styles of thought. Does this exhaust the space of cognition, or are there forms of "machine curiosity" and "new ways of thinking" that are native to the rulial space and orthogonal to human cognition?
prs.r: Wolfram's "machine curiosity and new ways of thinking" segment — argues that present-day AI is mining a small humanlike pocket of the Ruliad and that further progress requires AI systems whose curiosity and search dynamics are not constrained by human-imitation training
prs.s: A research-program suggestion that "AI's final form" is not a more-fluent humanlike system but a system exploring genuinely non-humanlike rulial regions — operationalizing the rulial-space-of-minds thesis as a specific research target rather than a metaphor

prs.label: P17 (PROP-2026-04-28-005 / src PROP-2026-04-27-005) — Three-parameter observer-class taxonomy
prs.p: The rulial-space-of-minds thesis (PRS-03, PRS-05) is conceptually compelling but has lacked concrete worked examples. Without specific observer-classes to point at, "different observers sample the Ruliad differently" remains a slogan rather than a research agenda
prs.r: Wolfram's three-parameter observer-class taxonomy (Last Theory #080): scale (molecule → planet), temporal coherence (instantaneous-state vs. light-delay-dominated), and multiway-coherence (single thread vs. multi-branch experience)
prs.s: A first-pass operational map of the rulial-space-of-minds: observer types are points in (scale × temporal-coherence × multiway-coherence) space, and each generates a distinct effective physics — converting PRS-03/05 from a programmatic claim into a research agenda

prs.label: P18 (PROP-2026-04-28-005, 2nd candidate) — Two-level reading of Principle of Computational Equivalence
prs.p: Does the Principle of Computational Equivalence (PCE) imply that all sufficiently complex observers think the same way, making observer-class differentiation a mere surface phenomenon? If yes, the rulial-space-of-minds thesis collapses
prs.r: Wolfram's argued resolution in #080: PCE applies to the *computational capability* of observers but not to the *experienced physics* of observers — two observers can be computationally equivalent and still inhabit incommensurable physics because they sample the underlying computation differently
prs.s: A clarified two-level reading of PCE: (i) computational-capability — all observers above the universality threshold are equivalent in what they can in principle compute; (ii) experiential-physics — those observers can still inhabit profoundly different effective worlds depending on sampling parameters. The rulial-spac…

prs.label: P19 (PROP-2026-04-28-006 / src PROP-2026-04-27-004) — Computational metaphysics as method-export to philosophy
prs.p: Wolfram's computational metaphysics has been challenged to engage rigorously with analytic philosophy. There is an unstated meta-question: must the computational program adopt analytic philosophy's methodology to count as having engaged it, or can it engage from outside that methodology?
prs.r: Wolfram's stated methodological self-description (Last Theory #081): the philosopher's mode of argument feels under-determined ("too much wiggling") relative to the discipline of running computational experiments; his engagement with philosophers is salonnière-style hosting, not internal adoption of philosophical meth…
prs.s: A reframing of the computational-metaphysics program as proposing a *new* methodology to philosophy — empirical ruliology applied to ontological questions — rather than as an attempt to satisfy analytic philosophy on its own terms. This converts the Jago/Seiberth dialogues from "compliance with philosophical scrutiny"…

prs.label: P20 (PROP-2026-04-28-006, 2nd candidate) — Computational cash-out as criterion for substantive metaphysical disagreement
prs.p: How does the Wolfram program adjudicate between competing philosophical accounts of its own central objects (the Ruliad, observers, emes) when those accounts use the formal vocabulary of analytic philosophy?
prs.r: Wolfram's implicit criterion in #081 — a philosophical formulation is taken seriously to the extent that it can be cashed out in or constrained by computational experiment; pure verbal/formal manipulation without computational cash-out is treated as the "wiggling" he distrusts
prs.s: A two-tier evaluation: (i) does the philosophical formulation produce a different prediction inside ruliology / observer theory? If yes, treat it as substantive. (ii) If no, treat it as one of many equivalent verbal frames over the same underlying computational structure

prs.p: What, computationally, is special about life — i.e., why do living systems orchestrate matter toward purposes rather than behaving like passive physical media, and is there any general (substrate-independent) characterization of "being adapted for a purpose"?
prs.r: "Bulk orchestration" + the "rulial ensemble" — the space of systems adapted for a given purpose, analyzed via the Principle of Computational Equivalence and computational irreducibility.
prs.s: A proposed universality result: for any "computationally simple" purpose, the systems that achieve it share certain behavioral features independent of the purpose's specifics — a candidate general law of adapted/living systems.

prs.p: Classical game theory analyzes optimal strategies for hand-selected programs (e.g., Axelrod's tit-for-tat tournament). Is there a principled best strategy for iterated competition, or is the selection of strategies-to-study itself unscientific?
prs.r: Ruliology of competition — treating strategies as programs and systematically enumerating ALL possible finite state machines / cellular automata / Turing machines, then running them against each other under fixed payoffs (matching-pennies, prisoner's dilemma, and the full space of 2-action games).
prs.s: There is generally no shortcut: which strategy wins is computationally irreducible, so one must run the competitions rather than prove a theorem. Wolfram's verdict directly challenges the "tit-for-tat / value of cooperation" conclusion as an artifact of looking only at submitted programs rather than the full strategy…

prs.p: When adaptive evolution discovers a winning strategy, can we describe the mechanism by which it wins?
prs.r: Adaptive evolution of finite-state-machine and cellular-automaton strategies under competitive pressure.
prs.s: Evolution reliably finds winning strategies, but typically as opaque "lumps of irreducible computation" that "just happen" to out-compete — there is no describable mechanism, mirroring Wolfram's account of biological evolution. Larger programs can also host "customized substrategies," exposing different rules to diffe…

prs.p: What distinguishes living systems from arbitrary computational systems? Wolfram's Physics Project derives universal physics from hypergraph rewriting, but life-as-computation has lacked a formal characterization that explains why some computations are alive and most are not.
prs.r: The "rulial ensemble" — a constrained ensemble of rules within rulial space, where the constraints are those that achieve and sustain organismic purpose. Combined with "bulk orchestration": the empirical observation that molecular and cellular processes are actively organized rather than statistically random.
prs.s: Life is a localized, history-dependent occupation of rulial space — an ensemble of rules selected, over evolutionary time, for the property that running them on each other produces a self-sustaining, self-correcting computational coherence. The rulial ensemble is to biology what a single rule is to physics.

prs.p: Computational irreducibility (PRS-04) seems to forbid prediction — yet biological organisms reliably reach developmental targets. How can adaptive, goal-directed systems exist within a universe where most computations are unpredictable?
prs.r: Bulk orchestration as the answer: organisms do not predict computational futures, they constrain them — the rulial ensemble is precisely the set of rules whose joint operation funnels otherwise irreducible computation into reliable, organism-scale outcomes.
prs.s: Biological reliability is not the negation of computational irreducibility but its harnessing. Selection acts on rule-ensembles whose collective behavior achieves bulk orchestration despite irreducibility at the substrate level. This reframes "agency" (PRS-04) as the local taming of irreducibility through rulial-ensem…

prs.p: The Wolfram Physics Project has been received with skepticism in mainstream physics partly because it appears to bypass the mathematical scaffolding (differential geometry, fiber bundles, gauge symmetry) that makes contemporary physics work. Without an articulation of how the hypergraph picture *contains* or *generali…
prs.r: The Madrid colloquium framing — "From Geometric Ideas to Computational Frontiers" — explicitly positions geometry and computation as complementary lenses on the same complex phenomena, with the hypergraph framework as the computational counterpart to the geometric one.
prs.s: A research-program move: Wolfram Physics is to be developed not as a replacement for geometric physics but as the substrate from which geometric physics emerges in the limit where rule-induced causal structure is dense enough to coarse-grain into a manifold. This is a programmatic commitment to interoperability with m…

prs.p: Wolfram's rulial-space / computational metaphysics is a framework. Translating it into practitioner-relevant claims about how to build AI systems is a separate challenge — the framework is large and abstract; the claims need to be concrete.
prs.r: The South Park Commons fireside chat as a venue where Wolfram is forced to compress the framework into actionable founder / engineer language.
prs.s: A practitioner-facing summary of what the rulial-space view recommends for AI system design — likely overlapping with but distinct from the Mullenweg critique. Useful for the wiki agent to track the gap between Wolfram-the-philosopher and Wolfram-the-tool-builder.

prs.p: Quantum algorithm speedups (Shor, Grover, etc.) are well-known cases of "quantum beats traditional," but the existing theoretical accounts (complexity classes, oracle separations) describe *that* such speedups exist without explaining *where in the structure of all possible computations* the speedup actually comes fro…
prs.r: Wolfram's framing in the April 24 Q&A: treat quantum algorithms as paths through the multiway/rulial graph that exploit branch-coherence (multi-thread sampling of the underlying hypergraph), and treat "classical algorithms" as observer-bounded single-thread paths. The speedup is then a structural feature of the observ…
prs.s: A ruliological reading of quantum advantage: classical-vs-quantum is the algorithmic shadow of single-thread-vs-multiway observer dynamics. Quantum speedup is the empirical signature, in computation, of the observer-class variation Wolfram has been describing in observer theory. This converts "why is quantum faster?"…

prs.p: Quantum biology (avian magnetoreception, photosynthesis, possibly olfaction) presents experimentally suggestive evidence that biological systems exploit quantum coherence, but lacks a unifying theoretical frame. Are these isolated curiosities, or are they instances of biology systematically inhabiting parts of the com…
prs.r: Wolfram's quantum-biology segment (Q&A April 24, opening ~20s): position biological systems as observers whose effective physics differs from human-scale observers along the (scale × multiway-coherence) axes of the PRS-17 taxonomy. Quantum-biological phenomena are then predicted not as exotic exceptions but as the *de…
prs.s: A bridge thesis: quantum-biological phenomena are the experimental signature of non-human-scale observer classes in Wolfram's observer-theory sense. This converts the patchwork of quantum-biology findings into a coherent prediction: *find more small-scale, multiway-coherent biological subsystems and you should find mo…

prs.p: How do paradigm-shifting ideas actually come about, and what organizational and leadership conditions favor them? Wolfram's computational-irreducibility thesis predicts that genuinely novel ideas cannot be reached by interpolation from existing positions — but does not by itself give a constructive account of where th…
prs.r: Wolfram's "Productive leadership & paradigm-shifting ideas" segment (~30 minutes, April 29, 2026 livestream) — first-person account from a paradigm-shifting practitioner of how he structures Wolfram Research, the Physics Project, and the Wolfram Institute around the conditions he believes generate paradigm-shifting id…
prs.s: A practitioner-level model of paradigm-shift generation (treating paradigm shifts as rulial-space jumps that require specific institutional scaffolding to be reachable), positioned as complementary to MacIntyre's tradition-internal mature-practitioner framework — the C2A2 tradition tracker can use this as a reference…

prs.p: The Wolfram program makes strong claims about AI's relationship to human cognition (PRS-11, PRS-12, PRS-15, PRS-16) but the *societal* and *business-structural* implications of those claims have been less explicitly articulated. How does Wolfram's rulial-space view of AI translate into practical claims about AI's impa…
prs.r: The "AI's impact on business & society" segment (April 29, 2026, t=11m44s, ~34 minutes) — Wolfram in a business-strategy register applying his computational framework to AI's role in firms and economies.
prs.s: A bridge document (potentially) between Wolfram's metaphysical/computational claims about AI (already in the wiki) and Wolfram's *applied* claims about AI's social and economic role — closing a small but real gap in the Wolfram wiki between the foundational essays and the practical implications. Useful for the master…

prs.p: Why does biology converge on brain-like structures specifically (rather than other possible information-integration substrates)? "Brains" as a biological category appears suspiciously load-bearing — but the Wolfram framework is supposed to be substrate-neutral. What does ruliology say about why brains, in particular,…
prs.r: Wolfram's segment "Why brains matter in biology" (Episode 167, t=18s) — applies the rulial-observer frame to the question of why centralized neural processing has the role it does in biological organisms, treating brains as a particular sampling structure within the rulial ensemble that biological evolution selects fo…
prs.s: A reading of "brains" as a class of high-coherence observer-structures within the rulial ensemble — not metaphysically privileged, but evolutionarily selected because of the kind of rulial-space sampling they enable. This converts "why brains?" from a biological mystery into a question about which observer-classes are…

prs.p: Standard evolutionary theory is bounded by biological substrate (DNA, cells, populations). Wolfram has begun arguing that the *form* of evolutionary process — variation, selection, lineage — is itself a substrate-independent rulial dynamic. But the C2A2 wiki has not yet captured a compact Wolfram statement of "evoluti…
prs.r: Wolfram's "Evolution beyond biology" segment (Episode 167, t=8m3s) — articulates evolution as a generic rulial-ensemble dynamic that biological evolution is one instance of, with implications for AI training, language change, and (by extension) MacIntyrean tradition-evolution.
prs.s: A programmatic statement that evolution is a *rulial process class* and biological evolution is a *specialization* — opening the door to applying Wolfram's evolutionary formalism to non-biological substrates (AI systems, traditions of inquiry, scientific paradigms) as legitimate ruliological objects rather than mere m…

prs.p: Who is accountable for the actions of autonomous, "ownerless" AI agents operating in the real world, when no single owner directs or can predict their behavior?
prs.r: Wolfram's computational-irreducibility account of agency (PRS-04): an agent's trajectory is not predictable from outside its own computation, so accountability cannot rest on the predictability or transparency of the agent's internal process.
prs.s: A reframing in which accountability attaches to the human–AI deployment-and-verification pipeline (who deploys, who verifies, who benefits) rather than to the agent's internal predictability — making "ownerless AI" a governance design problem about pipelines, not a search for a responsible internal homunculus.

prs.p: How can AI be made practically useful without users being "fooled" by confident-but-wrong output?
prs.r: The Computation-Augmented Generation / Foundation-Tool paradigm (PRS-11, PRS-13): symbolic computation as verifiable ground truth injected into LLM output; "computation and openness" as the missing deployment commitments.
prs.s: Deploy AI atop a computational verification backbone plus open infrastructure, so usefulness does not depend on trusting the LLM's self-report — extending the frontier-labs critique (PRS-13) from research strategy into practical deployment guidance.

prs.p: As AI accelerates the production of scientific claims and code, what becomes of the scientific method — how is genuine understanding preserved rather than merely accumulating unverifiable output?
prs.r: Wolfram's reframing of the scientific method under computational irreducibility plus AI: understanding as a bounded observer's compression of an irreducible computational world, with the method shifting toward computational experiment (ruliology) and formal/symbolic verification of results.
prs.s: A scientific method in which AI generates candidate results but trust attaches to a verification layer (symbolic/computational ground truth, extending CAG / PRS-11), and "understanding" is recast as the observer extracting reducible pockets from irreducible computation.

prs.p: How does human understanding itself change over time — is there a structure to the way understanding advances, or is it open-ended and ad hoc?
prs.r: The rulial-space-of-minds framing (PRS-03/05, PRS-15–18): understanding as movement of a computationally-bounded observer through rulial space; "evolving understanding" = traversal toward new reducible pockets of an irreducible structure.
prs.s: A model in which the growth of human (and machine) understanding is the progressive colonization of new regions of rulial space, making "how understanding evolves" a research question about observer trajectories rather than a purely historical narrative.

prs.p: Can AI-generated code be trusted, given that LLMs cannot guarantee correctness?
prs.r: "AI for verifying code" segment — pairing LLM generation with computational/symbolic verification as the reliability backbone.
prs.s: Relocate trust from generation to verification: the Wolfram computational stack (or any formal verifier) checks AI output, so usefulness does not depend on the LLM's own credibility. Direct extension of PRS-11 (CAG) and PRS-13 (computation + openness).

prs.p: LLM outputs are fluent but computationally untrustworthy — they hallucinate, can't guarantee exact results, and don't expose traceable steps. How can a symbolic-computation system supply the rigor LLMs lack without merely being another model to scale?
prs.r: Wolfram Agent Tools + the Version 15 MCP framework — a programmatic toolset, callable from within Wolfram Language and exposed to external AI clients (Claude, ChatGPT) via MCP, so an agent's reasoning chain can offload exact computation to deterministic Wolfram evaluation and receive traceable code/results back.
prs.s: A shipped architecture in which LLMs and symbolic computation are complementary rather than competing: the agent navigates/plans in rulial-space-as-language while exact, verifiable computational steps are delegated to the Wolfram backbone, each answer carrying its code and provenance.

prs.p: Encoding structured intellectual content (e.g., PRS triplets, cross-tradition relations) for agents to read and update requires a formally articulate, computable representation rather than free text — but such a representation must also remain executable and inspectable.
prs.r: Wolfram Language v15 as a symbolic, computable knowledge substrate now wired for agent invocation (Agent Tools + CAG + larger-than-2GB notebooks, expanded tabular/categorical data structures).
prs.s: A candidate infrastructure path for C2A2 itself — represent and manipulate tradition knowledge as computable symbolic objects an agent can both query and verify, rather than as opaque prose.

prs.p: Where are the boundaries of a mind? If two brains are linked (or a brain is emulated/copied), is there one observer or two — and what fixes the answer? Neuroscience frames this as connectivity; it lacks a principled criterion for observer individuation.
prs.r: Wolfram's observer-as-computational-persistence framework (PRS-12) plus the three-parameter observer-class taxonomy (PRS-17): an observer is a single coherent thread through the multiway graph, individuated by its temporal- and multiway-coherence parameters rather than by its physical substrate.
prs.s: Recast "one mind or two?" as a question about whether the coupled system maintains a single coherent thread of computational persistence (one observer) or two branches that fail to merge (two observers) — making mind-boundary a derivable property of observer-coherence structure rather than of neural wiring. Whole-brai…

prs.p: AI systems are beginning to produce genuine mathematical advances (e.g., a recent AI-assisted result on an Erdős problem). What would make such results trustworthy, and how common will they become?
prs.r: Wolfram's verification-over-generation stance (PRS-36/38, CAG / PRS-11): trust attaches to a computational/symbolic verification layer, not to the generating system's self-report.
prs.s: AI-assisted mathematical results become trustworthy to the extent they are cashed out into formally/computationally checkable steps; expect them to become common precisely where a verification backbone exists. This is an incremental extension of the existing AI-verification thread into the domain of AI-assisted mathem…

prs.p: Why do civilizations absorb some new scientific ideas quickly and leave others "ahead of their time" dormant for decades — what sets the uptake rate of a paradigm?
prs.r: Wolfram's historical survey of lost discoveries and idea-uptake dynamics (June 17 Q&A, segments at 0:18 and 12:10), read against his rulial-space framework: a community of observers occupies a region of rulial space, and an idea is absorbable only if a short rulial path connects it to the community's current sampling…
prs.s: Reframes "ahead of its time" as a measurable distance in concept-space rather than a romantic anomaly — the uptake rate of an idea is a property of the receiving community's position, not of the idea's intrinsic merit. Directly relevant to C2A2's tradition-accelerator premise: acceleration = engineering shorter paths.

prs.p: Could science reach a "final framework," and what would finishing fundamental physics actually terminate?
prs.r: Wolfram's June 17 discussion of a final framework (t=20m34s), grounded in computational irreducibility: even a complete rule for the universe leaves the behavior of most systems underivable except by running them.
prs.s: A final framework would end the search for the rule, not the practice of science — irreducibility guarantees an inexhaustible frontier of consequences. Science's endpoint is thus a category error; what ends is one kind of question, not inquiry itself.

prs.p: What is the evidential status of string theory after five decades without a distinguishing experimental confirmation?
prs.r: Wolfram's assessment of string theory's status and experimental evidence (June 17 Q&A, t=33m44s), delivered from outside the string program by the author of a rival post-spacetime framework.
prs.s: Positions string theory and the Wolfram Physics Project as facing the same confirmation problem — mathematical fertility without a distinguishing prediction — sharpening rather than evading the standard Carroll applies to Wolfram's own program.

prs.p: The discreteness of space is treated in the wiki as a Wolfram-originated postulate, leaving the program vulnerable to the charge that it is an idiosyncratic starting assumption rather than a live option with a genealogy.
prs.r: Wolfram's historical reconstruction of the discrete-space idea (segment 1, t=13s) — the lineage of proposals for space as a discrete network and the reasons continuum mathematics displaced them.
prs.s: Reframes hypergraph physics as the recovery and computational completion of a long-standing but under-tooled research option, rather than a novel postulate. Supplies the Wolfram Agent with a defensible answer to Carroll's status-assignment challenge (CROSS: "Does Wolfram Physics meet Carroll's Bayesian theory-confirma…

prs.p: How does a research program become part of the recognized history of a field — and what determines whether an idea ahead of its time is recovered or lost?
prs.r: Wolfram's account of historiographic method (segments 2-4): personal records as primary sources, the mechanics by which people and fields enter the canon, and material encounters with the past through machines and artifacts.
prs.s: A first-person, practitioner's model of tradition-formation and canonization, offered by a figure who is simultaneously a subject of it. Directly usable by the C2A2 master layer as source material on how traditions accumulate, preserve, and lose their own track records.

prs.p: Why are bugs ubiquitous and apparently ineliminable in any sufficiently capable software system — is this a contingent failure of engineering discipline, or a structural feature of computation itself?
prs.r: A ruliological account of bugs as instances of "the unexpected," grounded in a tradeoff between computational effectiveness and predictability: a program that reaches into computationally irreducible territory (and is therefore powerful) is for that very reason a program whose full behavior cannot be foreseen without…
prs.s: Bugs are the software-domain signature of computational irreducibility (PRS-04) — not a defect to be fully engineered away but a fundamental limit. Reliability is bought by deliberately confining a system to computationally reducible regions, at a direct cost in expressive reach. This converts "irreducibility limits p…

prs.p: Can software — including AI-generated code — be verified as correct, and how hard is exhaustive testing in general?
prs.r: The essay's analysis of what "a correct program" means and of the generic difficulty of exhaustive testing, tied to the same irreducibility argument and read against the tradition's existing verification-first paradigm (PRS-11 CAG, PRS-38, PRS-42).
prs.s: Adds a *bound* to the verification-over-generation thesis the wiki already records: verification remains the only reliable warrant, but its reach is itself limited when the target behavior is irreducible — exhaustive testing is generically hard, and a specification against which to check may not be finitely statable.…

prs.p: The framework explains why observers perceive *a* reality, but not why observers like us exist in the ruliad at all, nor what computationally distinguishes a mind from any other computationally-equivalent process such as weather or fluid turbulence.
prs.r: An input-compression criterion for observers-of-our-kind — an observer takes vast parallel input and crushes it down, at a very slow rate, to a single thread of next-action — combined with the Principle of Computational Equivalence, which denies that brains are computationally *more sophisticated* than weather and say…
prs.s: Observerhood becomes a structural rather than a sophistication property, and Wolfram now claims the existence and character of observers like us is "within sight of being able to derive scientifically" from the ruliad — converting the observer from a modelling assumption (PRS-01/05/12/17) into a derivable object, and…

prs.p: Why do computationally-bounded observers, each sampling the ruliad from its own location, agree that there is one objective world — and, in quantum mechanics, that one definite outcome occurred?
prs.r: Proximity-in-branchial-and-rulial-space plus *plurality*: observers construct objective reality by extrapolating that other observers' internal perceptions resemble their own, which works only because many similar observers sit close together in these spaces. Wolfram's night-sky analogy — we agree about the night sky…
prs.s: Objective reality (and definite quantum outcomes) is derived as an emergent consensus property of a *community* of nearby observers, not as a feature of the substrate. This is the tradition's first explicit account of intersubjectivity, and it makes shared world-making a physics-side result rather than a sociological…

prs.p: Is the apparent open-endedness of biological evolution a distinct biological phenomenon, or an instance of something more general?
prs.r: The machine-learning data point — Wolfram reports importing the 2010s empirical finding that heavily-trained neural nets do in fact learn, and applying the same schema to biological evolution by running simple computational systems under successive fitness objectives.
prs.s: Biological evolution and machine learning are claimed to be "extremely related kinds of things," both adaptive search in the computational universe; evolution never gets stuck because the space of simple programs always affords further complexity — the same principle used to explain free will under determinism. Sharpe…

prs.p: Every challenge this wiki records against the computational ontology is *internal to the method* — Carroll asks for a distinguishing prediction (PRS-45, Research Question 5), the string-theory comparison asks about confirmation debt. The tradition has no recorded encounter with a rival that grants the computational de…
prs.r: A public, moderated conversation with Iain McGilchrist at Ralston College, in which McGilchrist argues that reality has an "irreducible constitution" exceeding computation and that consciousness is grounded in embodiment, receptivity and participation — set directly against the simple-rules-underlying-complexity progr…
prs.s: Isolates a second challenge to the ruliad program, orthogonal to the prediction debt: the gap between *computational adequacy of description* and *ontological completeness*. The Carroll challenge can be met by producing a prediction; this one cannot, because it concedes the predictions. Naming it separately stops the…

prs.p: The tradition now carries a model of cross-paradigm idea-uptake — an idea is absorbable only if a short rulial path connects it to the receiving community's sampling position (PRS-43), and a shared objective world exists only among observers close together in branchial and rulial space (PRS-51) — but no case in which…
prs.r: The Ralston encounter itself, described by the host as "less a debate than an encounter," in which each party examines the other's foundational assumptions rather than trading conclusions, with no requirement that either concede.
prs.s: A self-application of the framework: on Wolfram's own account such an encounter should *not* converge, because two observers far apart in rulial space share no short path and no constructed objective world to appeal to — so the yield of the meeting is a map of the gap, not agreement. This converts Active Research Ques…

prs.p: Fundamental physics has accumulated a formalism tower deep enough that entry now requires years of prerequisite training, which closes the frontier to everyone outside the professional "priesthood" — while the appetite to contribute persists undiminished.
prs.r: Ruliology as a **low-prerequisite frontier** — a field young enough that "we're inevitably all at some level beginners in it," backed by Wolfram Language tooling in which every published figure is click-to-reproduce code.
prs.s: Redirect avocational effort from theory-of-physics attempts to systematic exploration of the computational universe, where an outsider can produce a genuinely novel, permanent result without traversing the physics tower. Wolfram commits to building the on-ramp: an educational program, a publishing venue, and a communi…

prs.p: What separates a contribution from a non-contribution, when the contributor lacks credentials? The received filter is social (credential, institution), which both excludes real outsiders and admits no procedure for the excluded to appeal.
prs.r: **Formalization in a computational language** as a credential-free admission test — the idea must be pushed "beyond pure words" into code the author can themselves understand with clarity.
prs.s: Replace the social filter with a procedural one. If an idea can be stated as executable computational language and run, it produces results, and the results either survive or do not — "that rule you found will always do that thing." Wolfram is explicit that this bar is high and that only a small fraction of the mail h…

prs.p: Do large language models lower the barrier to foundational scientific contribution?
prs.r: Wolfram's distinction between **AI as prose-generator** and **computation as heavy-lifting instrument**.
prs.s: A flat no on the first and a qualified yes on the second. An LLM handed an untrained idea will produce something with the surface form of a paper and near-certainly no coherence beneath it, *because* the idea was not already worked out somewhere in the training data for the model to read. Computation nevertheless help…

prs.p: Is the lone-genius model of discovery — flash of insight from nowhere — an accurate account of how paradigm-level advances happen?
prs.r: Historical audit of the standard cases plus Wolfram's own first-person account of the Physics Project.
prs.s: No, essentially without exception. Newton was already a senior professor; Einstein held a doctorate from a top university. Wolfram presents himself as the apparent counterexample — a CEO doing physics as a hobby — and then dismantles the reading: he was a professional physicist from his mid-teens, and the Physics Proj…

prs.p: Physics has no account of why time *passes* — why we experience an inexorable forward flow rather than a static block in which any moment is equally reachable.
prs.r: Computational irreducibility, plus the identification of a moment of time with one update step of the universe's rule.
prs.s: Time is redefined as "the irreducible doing of computation." The flow is not an extra ingredient added to physics; it is what it is like, from inside, for successive states to be computed one from the previous, in a case where no shortcut formula exists to jump ahead.

prs.p: If the universe follows a definite rule, why can a sufficiently clever observer not simply compute ahead and predict the future — and what stops time travel?
prs.r: The observer's own physical embedding: any computer an observer can build is itself made of universe-stuff and runs at the universe's own rate.
prs.s: A no-go boundary on embedded prediction. Wolfram's formulation: "You can't out-predict the universe from inside the universe." Prediction would require a substrate that steps faster than the substrate being predicted, and inside the universe there is no such raw material.

prs.p: Rule-governed determinism appears to leave no room for free will; if each state is fixed by the last, agency looks like an illusion.
prs.r: The distinction between determinism (the rule fixes the sequence) and predictability (someone can know the sequence in advance more cheaply than living it).
prs.s: Computational irreducibility severs the two. The external observer and the system "run at the same rate," so no one — including the agent — can outrun the process; "to see what's going to happen, you have to experience it." Wolfram then reads this positively: living through time performs an irreducible computation tha…

prs.p: What kind of thing must an observer be, for computational irreducibility to bite?
prs.r: Computational boundedness of observers, illustrated by encryption — a human cannot read an encrypted message by inspection and must instead try possibilities.
prs.s: Irreducibility only produces the experience of time for observers who are themselves computationally limited. The felt inexorability of time is therefore a joint property of the universe's rule *and* the observer's finite computational budget, not of the rule alone.

There is no source in the wiki in which Wolfram states his own open-problem list for the program, so the wiki cannot currently distinguish questions the program is actuall…

It would equally be evidence *against* the wiki if his list and this one barely overlap. Both outcomes ar…

prs.p: Wolfram's framework claims mathematics is *discovered within* the ruliad rather than invented — but that claim has never had an institutional research program attached to it, only essays. Without a program generating questions, the claim is untestable in Wolfram's own sense.
prs.r: The Wolfram Institute **Pure Math Project**, introduced publicly at ICM 2026.
prs.s: (Speculative) A standing program that treats pure-mathematical results as ruliological objects — enumerating axiom systems and entailment structures empirically, the way *P vs. NP and the Difficulty of Computation* (Jan 2026) treated complexity empirically rather than theoretically.

prs.p: Does the ruliology on-ramp thesis — that amateur and early-career researchers can do real science on simple computational systems (PROP-2026-08-15-001) — actually produce research, or is it aspirational?
prs.r: The 2026 Wolfram Summer Research Institute, reported complete with **50 original projects**, many aligned with Institute research directions.
prs.s: (Speculative) A yield figure for the on-ramp claim. 50 projects in one summer is the first countable output against that thesis.

prs.label: P1 (Text, p.407) — Hard problem of consciousness
prs.p: Consciousness cannot logically emerge from purely non-conscious matter; the hard problem is insurmountable under materialism
prs.r: Analytic Idealism’s inverted ontology: consciousness is primary, matter is its expression
prs.s: Idealism elegantly accommodates subjective experience, quantum phenomena, and anomalous cognition — dissolving rather than solving the hard problem by placing consciousness at the foundation

prs.label: P2 (Text, pp.102–103) — Individual identity within monism
prs.p: Individual beings appear as separate conscious entities, contradicting any monistic framework that posits a single universal consciousness
prs.r: Dissociative identity disorder as psychological model: a single consciousness with multiple dissociated points of view
prs.s: The universe as a single, undivided consciousness experiencing multiple dissociated points of view (individual beings) — preserving real individuality as “mental constructs arising from the dissociation process”

prs.label: P3 (Text, p.110) — Quantum anomalies under physicalism
prs.p: Quantum mechanics (wave-function collapse, observer-dependent reality) appears anomalous under physicalist frameworks — why does observation matter?
prs.r: Consciousness as foundational to reality: observation is not anomalous when the observer is ontologically primary
prs.s: Consciousness-first ontology elegantly explains quantum phenomena such as wave-function collapse and observer-dependent reality as natural features of a mental universe

prs.label: P4 (Implicit) — Bridging philosophy and mathematics
prs.p: Mathematical models of consciousness (Hoffman’s conscious agent theory) may lack philosophical grounding and interpretative coherence on their own
prs.r: Kastrup’s philosophical framework and dissociative psychology metaphors provide the narrative and conceptual layer
prs.s: Kastrup’s philosophical grounding deepens the interpretative layer of Hoffman’s mathematical model, enhancing narrative coherence — the CR paradigm requires both formal models and philosophical justification

prs.label: P5 (Implicit) — Empirical science seeking metaphysical foundation
prs.p: Neuroscience (McGilchrist), cognitive science (Hawkins), and active inference (Friston) develop rich empirical frameworks without addressing consciousness fundamentally
prs.r: Analytic Idealism as comprehensive metaphysical foundation: brains as correlates rather than generators of consciousness
prs.s: A unified philosophical interpretation of empirical brain models — Kastrup’s metaphysics philosophically grounds empirical findings that implicitly require a consciousness-first framework for full coherence

prs.label: P6 (Implicit) — Materialism as dialectical counterpart
prs.p: The conscious realist paradigm risks appearing as unfounded speculation without rigorous engagement with its most powerful critic (Carroll’s physicalism)
prs.r: Carroll’s poetic naturalism and physicalist critique as sharpening tool for conceptual clarity
prs.s: The conscious realist paradigm achieves intellectual integrity through sustained critical dialogue with rigorous materialism, not despite it — Carroll as indispensable dialectical partner

prs.label: P7 (PROP-2026-04-08-004) — Analytic Idealism applied to psychopathology
prs.p: Psychiatry faces a conceptual impasse: despite decades of neuroscientific research, mental disorders remain contested and therapeutically limited — indicating the underlying materialist framework may be insufficient
prs.r: Analytic Idealism's dissociation model applied clinically: mental disorders reframed as disturbances in the dissociative boundary between the individual alter and universal consciousness — not brain malfunctions but boundary dysregulation; published at Essentia Foundation, January 2, 2026
prs.s: A new interpretive framework enabling deconstruction of existing neuroscientific data under an idealist ontology, generating novel therapeutic hypotheses focused on boundary modulation — opening research directions unavailable under physicalism

prs.label: P8 (PROP-2026-04-08-007) — The Daimon as principle of individuation
prs.p: Analytic idealism risks appearing as unfounded speculation if it cannot account for why individuals have different characters, callings, and destinies — if all individual minds are alters of one universal consciousness, what explains the specificity and irreducibility of personal identity?
prs.r: Kastrup's "The Daimon and the Soul of the West" (Iff Books/Simon & Schuster, September 2025): the Daimon as the principle of individuation — each individual is not merely a generic dissociated alter but a specifically characterized one, with its own Daimonic signature
prs.s: A philosophically grounded account of personal identity, character, and vocation consistent with consciousness monism — the tension between "we are all one consciousness" and "I am irreducibly myself" is dissolved through the Daimonic model of patterned, meaningful dissociation

prs.label: P9 (PROP-2026-04-09-002) — Representation versus participatory encounter
prs.p: Kastrup's "dashboard of perception" metaphor — individual minds as screens presenting representations of universal consciousness — faces the objection that representation implies a mechanistic data-reading relation, missing the qualitative "participation" and genuine encounter that characterize lived conscious experie…
prs.r: Iain McGilchrist's counter-proposal (With Reality in Mind dialogue, April 7, 2026): perception is participatory, not representational — the perceiver is embedded in a field of consciousness, and the encounter is real two-way contact, not one-way display-reading
prs.s: Kastrup's analytic idealism may need refinement to distinguish two modes of "screening": (a) left-hemisphere mode (data-reading, representation, abstraction) — genuinely dashboard-like; (b) right-hemisphere mode (participation, encounter, embeddedness) — ontologically primary; this incorporates McGilchrist's hemispher…

prs.label: P10 (PROP-2026-04-15-005) — Idealism as empirical consciousness science framework
prs.p: Analytic idealism risks being dismissed as unfalsifiable metaphysics if it cannot engage productively with empirical neuroscience — specifically, it needs to show how consciousness-first ontology generates testable predictions that differ from physicalist alternatives
prs.r: The Koch-Kastrup dialogue (Essentia Foundation, February 20, 2026): Christof Koch's Integrated Information Theory provides empirically grounded consciousness science; the convergence of psychedelic experiences across individuals as a potential empirical window into shared consciousness substrate
prs.s: A possible bridge between IIT and analytic idealism: high-Φ states could correspond to porous dissociative boundaries; dissociation degree correlates with integrated information measurements — making idealism testable against IIT while respecting both frameworks' empirical rigor

prs.label: P11 (PROP-2026-04-15-004) — Continuation of idealist time debate
prs.p: If time is illusory within analytic idealism (time is a representation in universal consciousness, not ontologically real), then the traditions that humans participate in — with their genuine historical depth and cross-generational transmission — lack ontological grounding beyond phenomenal appearance
prs.r: Second Kastrup-McGilchrist dialogue (With Reality in Mind, April 14, 2026) — continuing the tensions identified in the April 7 session, expected to develop the representation/participation debate and introduce the daimon concept as a bridge between systematic and personal philosophy
prs.s: For analytic idealism to support C2A2's tradition-accelerator project, Kastrup may need to develop an account of why temporal structure of traditions is not merely illusory — perhaps via the argument that patterned dissociation (the alter's structure) is itself temporal in a way that is real within universal conscious…

prs.label: P12 (PROP-2026-04-22-002) — Bernardo Kastrup on the state of the consciousness debate
prs.p: Analytic idealism is often received as one metaphysical option among many (physicalism, panpsychism, IIT, dual-aspect monism) without a clear articulation from Kastrup of what specifically distinguishes his position from each rival, and where the live disagreements versus terminological disagreements lie
prs.r: A "state of the debate" long-form interview (March 2026) in which Kastrup maps the current consciousness conversation explicitly and positions analytic idealism against each major rival, likely including updated commentary post-Koch dialogue
prs.s: A synthesized articulation of analytic idealism's distinctive claims versus (a) physicalism — the hard problem is insurmountable, (b) panpsychism — combination problem remains unsolved, (c) IIT — Φ is a correlate, not a cause, (d) dual-aspect monism — unnecessary duplication; providing the C2A2 master wiki with a comp…

prs.label: P13 (PROP-2026-04-27-013) — Explanation vs Computation — Q&A with Bernardo Kastrup
prs.p: Computational and predictive models of reality (including ruliological / physicalist programs) routinely substitute simulation for explanation — leaving the question of whether they track reality unanswered.
prs.r: An explicit demarcation criterion — *explanation* (accounting for why the phenomenon must be so) vs. *computation* (predicting that the phenomenon is so) — as the test for whether a metaphysics is realism-eligible.
prs.s: An epistemological filter that sharpens the analytic-idealism program: idealism is preferred because it minimizes the residual brute-fact / explanatory-gap remainder, not because of greater predictive scope.

prs.label: P14 (PROP-2026-05-13-004) — Kastrup-Levin dialogue on dissociative-boundary individuation
prs.p: Analytic idealism's DID-derived account of individuation (PRS-02) has not been clear about whether the dissociative-boundary mechanism permits the kind of fine-grained, scale-continuous nesting of conscious agents that Levin's program requires (cells → tissues → organs → organisms → constructs), or whether dissociativ…

prs.s: A sharpening of analytic idealism's individuation claim — Kastrup must specify what determines a dissociative boundary (and therefore which biological/computational systems qualify as alters), or accept that Levin's gradient is compatible with idealism if "alter" is read more permissively. Either move is a substantive…

prs.p: The C2A2 network treats Kastrup and Levin as broadly aligned within the consciousness-as-fundamental cluster, but no extant C2A2 source has clearly articulated where the two diverge inside that cluster — leaving the network with a possibly false impression of unanimity.
prs.r: A long-form, two-thinker dialogue in which the live disagreement is the explicit subject — providing the canonical citation for any future C2A2 discussion of how Kastrup and Levin stand relative to one another.

prs.p: Whether AI agents have subjective vantage points becomes a load-bearing engineering question for C2A2, but neither Kastrup's discrete-alter view nor Levin's continuous-nesting view straightforwardly settles it.
prs.r: The dialogue's treatment of constructed agents — Levin's openness to AI as candidate site of subjective perspective; Kastrup's caution that AI may lack the dissociative structure that defines an alter.

C2A2 can defer the AI-membership question to that boundary-individuation criterion rather than treat i…
